rationale: Closed the client-completion account with the corrected-admission receipt: both declared comparisons hold, so the re-queue and the subsequent completion are measured rather than derived. The question's disposition is set to explained, the superseded unknown outcome is retained with its cause, and the re-propose behavior now cites all three receipts.

knowledge.statement: handleCommit, for the instance owner only, tests whether the committed command is a single NONE operation and whether the local leader bookkeeping still holds pending client proposals; when both hold it pushes every pending proposal back onto the replica's own ProposeChan and clears lb.clientProposals, so the client request is re-proposed on a new instance instead of being consumed by the committed NOOP. The re-queued proposal keeps the same command id and reply writer, and the new instance's decision and execution deliver the client reply, while the replaced instance itself produces no reply because its proposals were cleared.
knowledge.conditions: A commit that decides a single NOOP for an instance owned by the local replica while that replica still holds client proposals for it (epaxos/epaxos.go:1082-1100, reached after a recovery replaced the owner's accepted command).

interpretations.rationale: Current account: the completion contract survives a recovery that replaces the owner's command, and both declared comparisons now hold on a corrected admission. Receipt 893f6180a4514a8d9e20a1d5e6698542 (fixed experiment 6fbba03eb3354cf384e0044c37ac7542-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryReproposesClientRequest, exit 0, 19 parsed events, no diagnostics): comparison 0 holds at index 11 (requeued 1, pending_proposals 0, reply_bytes 0) and comparison 1 holds at index 17 (the completion reply carries command id 77 for instance (0,1)); the supporting events are index 10 (the pending proposal with command id 77 re-queued while the owner's instance holds the replacement NOOP), index 13 (the re-queued proposal becoming instance (0,1) through the replica's own propose path), index 14 (that instance decided at status COMMITTED), index 15 (the commit broadcast) and index 16 (the package's own execution entry point returning true with 17 reply bytes). The earlier receipt f96da636a32f473280ce82dc0f0a002d (fixed experiment 602b7dcab8064d2ab9113ac315a40743-experiment) supplies the same scenario's first half: the owner holds command X at index 2, its own prepare reply for the recovery carries that command at index 3, the recovering replica 3 proposes the NOOP at indices 6 and 7 although it holds no command, the recovered decision replaces the owner's instance at index 9, and the re-queue follows at index 10 with reply_bytes 0 at index 11. Receipt e5527cca0ee64fd681d3ec1371f9cca6 is retained as the superseded attempt whose completion comparison returned unknown because its admission event described instance (0,0) while the reply observation describes instance (0,1) - an observation-construction defect of the harness, corrected by the current experiment; its event stream already contained the same reply. Source basis: handleCommit re-queues the owner's pending proposals and clears them (epaxos/epaxos.go:1090-1098), and the execution path emits a reply only for an instance whose executing replica still holds proposals (epaxos/exec.go:126-138) - which is why the replaced instance itself yields no reply and the client's completion is served by the re-proposed instance. No defect is claimed for this relationship: the replacement is paired with a re-offer and a later completion, at the cost of one extra instance and a delayed reply.

ed76b573b9fe4bde9565d4b4678cda85-gap-1.explanation: The replaced instance itself produces no client-visible reply: replies are emitted only by the execution path and only while the executing replica still holds client proposals for the executed instance (epaxos/exec.go:126-138), and handleCommit cleared the owner's pending list when the replacement decision arrived - measured as pending_proposals 0 and reply_bytes 0 in receipt f96da636a32f473280ce82dc0f0a002d (index 11). The client's completion is served by the re-proposed instance: receipt 893f6180a4514a8d9e20a1d5e6698542 shows instance (0,1) decided at index 14 and its execution writing a 17-byte reply carrying command id 77 at indices 16 and 17.

counterevidence: The re-propose path is gated on three conditions in handleCommit (owner row, a single NONE command, non-nil pending proposals); a replacement decision carrying a non-NONE command, or an instance owned by a failed replica, leaves the client request un-reproposed, which is the path the committed-value experiment documents.
Both measured paths required the owner to stay alive; the completion is not available when the owner is the failed replica.

The completion depends on the harness invoking the package's own execution entry point directly: no run() loop or executeCommands goroutine existed, so the scheduling of that call (and hence the reply's timing) is the harness's rather than the target's.

The first execution of the extended harness returned unknown for the completion comparison even though its event stream contained the reply with command id 77; that outcome was an admission-identity defect of the observation, not evidence about the target, and is superseded by the current experiment.
limitations: One command shape (single PUT), one key, two instance indices and one alive owner; the batching case, where the re-propose loop pushes several proposals for one instance, was not exercised.
The reply was decoded from the proposal's reply writer inside the harness rather than over a client socket, and the execution entry point was called synchronously.
The completion's timing (one extra proposal round) was not measured: the harness drove the second proposal immediately instead of waiting for a client retry or the executor's own cadence.
